CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/03/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 1001094
Permit API: 015-23770
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/07/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Cummings Lumber" Marcellus well site.Repsol finished drilling the 6 new Marcellus wells at this site in April 2023.There are 5 previously existing Marcellus wells at this site. 4 are in production and 1 is plugged. JD Ressler called the DEP on July 3, 2023 to report an unknown quantity release of produced liquid dripped from a vac truck onto the access road for this site. I spoke with JD Ressler (Repsol) on site. He explained that the vac truck dripped produced liquid about half way up the access road. A driver behind the vac truck noticed the leak. The vac truck stopped and they closed the partially open valve. Repsol immediately scraped the moist material off the road and put it in a 55 gallon drum. Andrew Senefelder (Repsol) emailed to inform they estimate 6.8 gallons of production liquid leaked from the truck onto the access road. Repsol removed approximately 4 cubic yards of road material and placed it it a 55 gallon drum awaiting disposal. I did not see any residual liquid or moist soil on the access road. Violations cited to the 015-23770 permit are considered immediately corrected. ProFrac started hysdraulically fracturing the 6 new Marcellus wells at this site on June 21, 2023.Vegetation, rock, and erosion blanket stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface.Air temp 80FJLP

Permit API: 015-23861
Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On 06/04/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) received a spill notification (CTS 389602) for Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) Kerrick Unit Well Pad in Asylum Township, Bradford County. Steve Moyer stated a stain was found on the pad around 1000 hours. It was discovered that stormwater mixed with produced water either overtopped the containment or there is a hole in the containment. It was estimated ~ 20 gallons were released. The stain is ~ 40' x 44' x 50' off containment. On 06/05/2025 the DEP conducted an incident inspection at the Kerrick Unit Well Pad in Asylum Township, Bradford County. The weather was 78 degrees and sunny. I arrived at 0915 hours. Expand representative Mike Deming accompanied me during the inspection. Mike stated that water in the area of the discovered release was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 7-8 mS/cm. The soil was also field measured for EC ~ 4 mS/cm. There was no pooled water on the pad at the time of the inspection. Mike stated on 06/04/2025 some material was recovered and placed in a lined dumpster onsite (photo #3-5). Approximately six inches of material was scraped. Remediation will resume once the produced fluid tank is removed. The produced fluid tank will be removed either today or tomorrow. Further investigation and remediation will be continued after that.Due to the unknown volume of the release the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 for compliance. Based on the reported release the following violations are cited against API #015-23861:35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/11/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 981697
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/11/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after the reported release of produced fluid to the northeast corner of Pad B and to the north stormwater channel on 12/19/22. I met with Matt Covine, Zachary Subra, and Rick Hall all of EQT during this inspection. On Pad B the sump remains installed at the northeast corner of the north stormwater channel. The fluid in the sump has an electrical conductivity (EC) of 2.07 mS/cm. A visible path was observed from the northeast edge of the sump to the farthest line of compost filter sock near the site limit-of-distance (LOD). This had not been observed in any previous inspection. Mr. Subra took an EC reading of the soil at the end of the path in front of the compost filter sock and it was 300 uS/cm. Multiple puddles of fluid were found north and northwest of the MASS. The EC of this fluid ranged from 2.62 mS/cm to 7.70 mS/cm. I took sample number 0718-199 from the puddles northwest of the mass and north of the secondary containment for the parking area of the super sucker vacuum truck.The fluid in the containment to the east of the MASS is approximately 2 mS/cm. The Department recommends emptying the containment. A line that brings fluid from the gas busters at the produced fluid offload area and puts it into the MASS appeared to still have a slow leak. A tray was underneath this area along the line which had what appeared to be an oily substance in it. The Department recommends ensuring that this does not leak onto the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming up any and all puddles found in the vicinity of the MASS until the 12/19/22 release is remediated. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum out the sump at the end of the stormwater channel. The Department recommends repairing or replacing the line of damaged compost filter sock near the sump. The Department recommends reporting any additional developments regarding the MASS release to the Department including elevated electrical conductivity puddles found in a new area on the pad surface. Violations remain outstanding for the 12/19/22 reported release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad B.

Violation ID: 8267701
Permit API: 051-21986
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2026
Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Gabonay National City Bank 6 well in response to the operator's submission of a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well. This inspection is being separated into 3 inspection reports due to the number of photos taken. The narrative of all 3 inspection reports are identical except for the references to photos. This is inspection report 1 of 3.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced. E and S plan is present on-site at the mailbox at the beginning of the access road.Well is tagged and posted. Production tank is observed within an adequately vegetated berm at this time. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at this time. The RCE is not installed as depicted on the plans. Minimal gravel is observed, which appears to be pre-existing. The access road does not appear to be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plans calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary." Four locations on the access road are experiencing erosion and sedimentation off of the access road (Photos 10-13, 18). CFS is also not observed in these locations despite the E and S plan call for CFS installed "as needed."There are 8 culvert crossings observed during today's inspection. Some ends of the culverts are blocked due to what appears to be recent soil and vegetation clearing off the access road. Some of the culvert crossings appear to possibly be stream crossings. A follow up inspection is being requested with Department Biologists to identify possible streams and/or wetlands. CFS is not observed to be installed at any of the culvert crossings except for the last culvert crossing closest to the site. The CFS at this crossing appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time, but is only installed on one side of the crossing. The E and S plans on site do not delineate or identify any stream or wetlands or crossings of any streams or wetlands, and no 105 permits are observed on site or at any of the crossings at this time. The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.CFS is observed to be installed on-site near the well and appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time. The location of the CFS appears to be placed in the correct area in relation to the site's topography, however the E and S plans depict the CFS to be placed on the opposite (East) side of the site. A small channel of stormwater appears to be leaving the site and passing through CFS at this time, however no sediment is observed leaving the site. The Department recommends the operator monitor and maintain this area as necessary to ensure CFS continues to function properly. Plastic matting is observed to be installed in 3 locations along the access road.The Department recommends the operator redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.Violations are being issued for accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending consultation with Department Biologists.

Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2026
Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Gabonay National City Bank 6 well in response to the operator's submission of a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well. This inspection is being separated into 3 inspection reports due to the number of photos taken. The narrative of all 3 inspection reports are identical except for the references to photos. This is inspection report 1 of 3.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced. E and S plan is present on-site at the mailbox at the beginning of the access road.Well is tagged and posted. Production tank is observed within an adequately vegetated berm at this time. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at this time. The RCE is not installed as depicted on the plans. Minimal gravel is observed, which appears to be pre-existing. The access road does not appear to be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plans calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary." Four locations on the access road are experiencing erosion and sedimentation off of the access road (Photos 10-13, 18). CFS is also not observed in these locations despite the E and S plan call for CFS installed "as needed."There are 8 culvert crossings observed during today's inspection. Some ends of the culverts are blocked due to what appears to be recent soil and vegetation clearing off the access road. Some of the culvert crossings appear to possibly be stream crossings. A follow up inspection is being requested with Department Biologists to identify possible streams and/or wetlands. CFS is not observed to be installed at any of the culvert crossings except for the last culvert crossing closest to the site. The CFS at this crossing appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time, but is only installed on one side of the crossing. The E and S plans on site do not delineate or identify any stream or wetlands or crossings of any streams or wetlands, and no 105 permits are observed on site or at any of the crossings at this time. The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.CFS is observed to be installed on-site near the well and appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time. The location of the CFS appears to be placed in the correct area in relation to the site's topography, however the E and S plans depict the CFS to be placed on the opposite (East) side of the site. A small channel of stormwater appears to be leaving the site and passing through CFS at this time, however no sediment is observed leaving the site. The Department recommends the operator monitor and maintain this area as necessary to ensure CFS continues to function properly. Plastic matting is observed to be installed in 3 locations along the access road.The Department recommends the operator redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.Violations are being issued for accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending consultation with Department Biologists.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 08/19/2020
Comments: On 08/19/2020 DEP representatives John Ciccone and Korey Starkey (Water Quality Specialist) conducted an incident inspection on Chesapeake's Ferraro location at 1000 hours. This inspection was in response to a spill notification (CID # 351908) received the early morning of 08/19/2020. The spill notification stated that at 0400 hours, a gas kick resulted in a release of 2.5 barrels of oil based mud from the well head. Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake) estimated that 1.5 barrels sprayed on containment and 1 barrel sprayed off containment.At the time of arrival (1000 hours), we met with Eric Hottenstein at the pad entrance. Mr. Hottenstein explained that crews were currently mustered outside and that lines were shut-in. At approximately 1015 hours, Jon Zwetzig (Chesapeake Field Safety Representative) met with us and stated we were allowed back onsite along the perimeter of the pad. Mr. Zwetzig and Mr. Hottenstein led us toward the southern edge of the pad where the oil based mud sprayed off containment. From the point of the spraying event to the edge of containment was approximately 100' (photo # 2, 3). An additional 60' of vegetation had been excavated from the southern edge of the pad out toward the tree line (photo # 5). The gas kick took place while drilling the 5H well according to Mr. Zwetzig.According to Mr. Hottenstein, the majority of the sprayed oil based mud was captured by the dense vegetation off of the southern edge of the pad, with visually minimal oil based mud making contact with the ground (photo # 13). A dark staining was visually observed on the vegetation along the existing tree line that remained to be excavated (photo # 7, 8, 10, 13) and the smell of oil was heavy along the impacted treeline. Mr. Hottenstein stated that Chesapeake plans to continue excavating the impacted vegetation and then soil samples are to be taken from the roughly 60' x 60' excavated location (photo # 12). Sampling is to be conducted by Creston Environmental. Excavated vegetation and materials are being staged within containers at the Mad Dog lcoation, where additional plastic liner is being laid down for containment.Mr. Hottenstein stated that once excavation and soil sampling is completed, the excavated grounds will be hydroseeded and additional silt sock will be laid down gradient in order to mitigate any potential erosion and sedimentation.Mr. Hottenstein stated that Chesapeake will be pursuing Act 2 remediation.The release of a regulated substance to the ground surface is in violation of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and Chapter 78a.56(a). Due to an undetermined amount of regulated substance being released to the ground surface, please refer to 78a.66 regarding remediating releases of regulated substances on well sites.We departed the site at 1100 hours.

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2023
Comments: On 6/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Solowiej well site. It was 65 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. I did not screen for conductivity because I did not witness any water puddles or muddy areas on the pad surface during the inspection.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by one sediment pond. The sediment pond is adequately stabilized and was dry at the time of the inspection. I was able to witness an 8 inch riser sticking up about 16 inches from the pond surface. The outlet for the sediment pond overflow drains into a stream alongside the River View roadway. This stream drains to the waters of the Commonwealth. Following an inspection conducted on 10/18/2022, Chesapeake reported that it would make changes to the site to mitigate the issues with the sediment pond. They reported that they were developing a design to accommodate both the drainage and the land owner and hoped to have a finalized plan with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features. There are outstanding violations against the outfall coming off the sediment pond. There were three wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment.The DEP recommends that Chesapeake continues with the process to obtain a revised ESCGP application with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features and submit to the Department for review.I left the site at 1400 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: Mercer Borough
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/05/2023
Comments: Routine field inspection performed in the afternoon with cold, overcast clouds with snow flurry weather conditions and 36 degrees. Last inspection performed on 3/22/2018, more than 5 years ago. Wellhead is located in an open, partially maintained field area ~70' South of surface/ground production equipment in close, visible proximity. At the wellhead surface casing valve is open, lower right side production tubular valve open to ports and drip/domestic house gas meter run with port valves closed, open valve to drip and open supply valve after meter, lower production tubular left side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with no valve unions, and the production tubular plumbed on left side of head (opposite meter) to sales/surface equipment has closed valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photos #1 and #2). Meter reading (photo #3). Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead (photo #4). Some fair corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility and one 100 bbl steel tank all contained by an earthen dike (photo #5). Valve cracked open on main tubular feeding facility/separator with open valves to and from separator (photo #6). A 31-day production chart is present with no distinct markings only an ink blob mark and dated 1/2/23, which is nearly one year ago (photo #7). A pipeline, MRM 3200 is located adjacent, just North of surface production facility (photo #8). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except Operator contact address. The well posting details are difficult to read, accurately and the Department requests well posting be replaced to include Operator address information and more legible details (photo #9). Trace to occasionally fair corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Operator submitted 2022 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well stating 355 psig. The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2022 is blank and indicates that this well was not in production during the 2022 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having blank production under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the '22, '21, '20, and '19 annual production reports. The last reported production was in 2018 with 568 Mcf recorded over 365 days. During todays inspection, OGI spoke to the land/home owner who stated that house gas is not being provided currently and has not been provided in many years. Given this information and todays inspection, the well is abandoned and has not been operational in over 4 years. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well abandonment OGA3220(A). Well location and facility field verified and GPS coordinates of wellhead updated with this inspection showed a minimal distance offset of ~42ft between coordinates (photo #10). This is not an active, producing well. The well is abandoned and not providing house gas to the land/home owner.

Comments: On 05/01/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLCs Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 0930 hours, weather was 62F and sunny. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Standing water observed on the pad surface field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~246-645us/cm.There are 2 wells tagged with American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers located onsite (photos #2 and 3). Personnel were onsite drilling top holes and setting conductors for 3 additional wells; they informed me that rig move in for well drilling would begin on approximately 05/15/2025. (photo #4). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #5). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which held less than 10% standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #6); the containment structure contained less than 10% standing water. A dehydration unit is also noted and held in secondary containment (photo #7).Numerous temporary storage tanks are located onsite and contain produced fluids from flow back (photos #8 and 9). The temporary storage tanks are held in secondary containment. The upright brine storage tanks remain onsite and have been confirmed to be empty by personnel at Greylock (photo #10). Roll-off waste containers were also observed onsite and contain top hole drilling cuttings (photo #11).Areas surrounding the site are not yet permanently stabilized with greater than 70% uniform perennial vegetative cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. An erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review and up to date (photo #12). 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #13). No standing water was observed in the PCSM controls and they appear to be functioning as intended.Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962 pending receipt of confirmation sampling and approval of Act 2 remediation standards.No violations noted. I departed the site at 1030 hours.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of the Kingsley E pad on 6/16/2022 at 1102. The weather was 71 degrees and overcast. DEP Water Quality Specialist Korey Starkey assisted with the inspection.This inspection was conducted to assess current site conditions and evaluate what remedial work has been conducted. It appears that a majority of the pad surface has been excavated. Lined roll-off tanks with impacted material collected from clean up are present on the pad. These roll-off tanks are then being removed for proper disposal offsite. Company personal onsite were continuing excavating for cleanup and a vacuum truck was present to contain any fluids. The DEP recommends extending clean up efforts to areas just off the pad surface that may have collected significant amounts of drainage. The CSL 402(b) violation cited against API# 015-23678 on 6/6/2022 remains outstanding at this time. Additional violations are considered pending awaiting sample results 4406-014 and 9558-001. Permit API: 123-48606
Unconventional: No

Comments: I conducted a routine inspection of the Allshouse Fraser 1001 well, this well was stimulated yesterday. The road surface did not hold up to the increased traffic as heavy mud and significant ruts are present. Accelerated erosion of the road surface is taking place, a spring run with steady flow is present and running down the road due to lack of a culvert or other BMP to carry the water across the road. The spring left the road ditch and ran down the road approximately 300 feet before reentering a road ditch. The sediment laden water then traveled through a cross culvert before being discharged over the hillside above Route 6. The water then ran an additional 200 feet over the hillside and into the storm drain on the east bound lane of Route 6. From there the sediment laden water continued to the storm sewer outfall above the river and entered into the Allegheny River. The plume of sediment water remained for approximately 30 feet along the south bank of the Allegheny River.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation ID: 970190
Permit API: 039-25765
Unconventional: Yes
County: Crawford
Municipality: North Shenango Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/27/2022
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint ID #366445 that is dated 8/22/2022.The complainant indicated to the Department that they had concerns regarding the installation of a stormwater discharge pipe at the site. It was stated that the stormwater basin recently overtopped and flooded the adjacent township roadway. Based upon the information from the complainant the operator installed a new discharge pipe that outlets to the roadside ditch of the township road. The ditch flows into UNT to Bennett Run (WWF).Based upon my investigation and site inspection the Department finds the following: -It appears that the sediment basins did overflow and discharge stormwater into the woods and out onto the township road.Recent activity indicates:-The two sediment basins have been cleaned out of sediment.-An earth berm along the wood line has been established between the two basins.-A graded channel/swale has been created between the basins. The southern basin flows through the swale to the northern basin.-There are several rock filters within the swale/channel.-It appears that a 4" PVC pipe has been installed from the northern basin and day lights to the roadside ditch of the township road. (Currently flowing water)The recent activity at the site regarding the post construction stormwater management of the site was not approved by the Department. Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to inspection 2995415 in which violations where noted for accelerated erosion rills along the access road and exposed soil on and adjacent to the well site. Assisting with this inspection is PADEP Eric Norman and operator representative Isaac Haky is also present. The operator appears to have regraded the access road and placed stone at various locations along the artery leading to the well site. However, because some portions of the access road do not appear to have been stabilized these rock sections are acting as RCE and accumulating sediment on top of them (Photo #8). The operator has placed straw at the discharge point on either side of the access road and it appears that a CFS is not installed correctly with wooden stakes and blown/placed filter media absent (Photo #1). The operator has temporarily stabilized excess soil material from resurfacing the access road, along the access road (Photo #9). The Department requests information from the operator regarding what the operator intends on doing with that material as well as calculations for how much earth disturbance has been conducted at the site during this process (from 02/10/2020 to 03/11/2020) to include the entirety of the access road network. The operator appears to have regraded the bare spot adjacent to the well site and applied straw to that location and where the water was running off the site and into the vegetated area (Photo #2, 4, & 5). However, there appears to be several spots on the well site that do not have adequate coverage to resist accelerated erosion (Photo #3 & 6). The Department recommends that the operator install CFS per the E&S Manual Standard Construction Detail 4-1 to ensure the BMP works as intended. The Department recommends that the operator take steps to prevent accelerated erosion or sedimentation by stabilizing the access road and site. Based on this inspection the violations for this site will remain outstanding. Based on responses received from the operator more violations may be issued.

Comments: This unconventional well is currently equipped for production and is equipped with a well tag displaying the well’s API number. The site ID sign at the entrance of the pad includes the required information, however it has become faded. Drilling operations were completed on this well on 8/21/2011. There is a second active well (047-24580) on this pad for which drilling operations were completed on 7/20/2011. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0021 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling the last permitted well on this well site. Approximately one-half of this pad does not appear to be actively used for the operation of this well. There are four steel tanks labeled as holding production water located inside of a lined steel containment on this well site. At this time, the containment appears sound, as it is holding several inches of stormwater. A well development impoundment (Impoundment # 5) is located approximately 900’ northeast of the HM1 well site. This impoundment is covered by the same ESCGP that encompasses the HM1 well site. The Department does not have record showing that this well development impoundment has been registered, as is required by Chapter 78a.59b(b). The water from this impoundment is currently being discharged via a 2" plastic pipe out of the southwest corner of the impoundment onto a vegetated swale. There are currently no surface concerns evident from this dewatering. The access road leading to this well site and well development impoundment is in general holding up to current traffic levels. Routine maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road to prevent potential E&S issues. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site & well development impoundment, as well as the access road banks appears to be established. Future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site & well development impoundment.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/28/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8286873
Permit API: 081-21212
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/28/2026
Comments: On August 28, 2026, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response inspection at the Range Resources Laurel Hill Well Pad B. Range Resources Kirby Steck reported on August 27, 2026 at 2135, a gasket for a filter pod failed causing a release of reuse water outside of containment. The filter pod was associated with a WMGR123 onsite supporting the Bear Hollow Well Pad stimulation. Upon arriving onsite, Range Resources had initially estimated the spill to be 15 to 20 gallons. When the DEP arrived onsite, Range Resources contractor had begun excavating the area of the fill slope of the well pad impacted by the release. The area of excavation at the time of arrival was approximately 10 feet by 10 feet and about 18 inches deep. Soil conductivity of the impacted area ranged from 3,000 to 6,000 uS/cm. Range Resources contractor continued to excavate the area of impact during the inspection. The area of impact had increased to approximately 20 feet by 10 feet and approximately 3 feet in depth. At 3 feet depth, Range Resources was finding elevated soil conductivity levels of 6,000 uS/cm. Prior to the DEP leaving the site, Range Resources determined that they would proceed with remediating the spill through the Act 2 process due to the spill being larger than initially estimated.Violations of Chapter 78a.56(a), Clean Streams Law 402(b), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted due to the release of reuse water outside of secondary containment onto the well pad slope.
